note: ⚠️ SNG-286 (Erik): 'think about how players should/could earn titles as they play - could be earned in certain domains or in the world... or locally or all.' TITLES ARE WHAT THE WORLD CALLS YOU, and the world already has the machinery: `recordDeed` carries tags/weight and `spreadDeeds` walks a deed community by community. A TITLE IS A DEED PATTERN THAT TRAVELLED FAR ENOUGH TO BECOME A NAME.

theScopeLadder.note: ⚠️ SCOPE IS NOT PRESTIGE — IT IS REACH. Erik's four scopes map exactly onto how far the deeds spread. A local title is not a lesser title; it is a title that one place means and nowhere else has heard.

local.flavour: they call you this in one town. It is the most personal kind and the easiest to lose by leaving.

regional.flavour: a reach knows you. This is where a title starts arriving ahead of you.

domain.reach: a tradition, anywhere it is practised
domain.spread: >= 6 across >= 2 regions, deeds tagged to one tradition
domain.flavour: ⚠️ THE MOST INTERESTING SCOPE: known to your CRAFT rather than your geography. A Grave-Caller is known to Ashwardens in reaches they have never visited, and unknown to the farmers next door.

world.flavour: the Valley knows the name. Roughly a sixth of all communities — rare, and it should be.

howTitlesAreEarned.principle: THE WORLD NAMES YOU; YOU DO NOT CLAIM IT. Same doctrine as earned backgrounds — rung 2, 'grant what the story conferred.' A player cannot ask for a title and the engine must refuse if they do.
howTitlesAreEarned.mechanism: a title fires when a DEED PATTERN (tag + minimum weight + count) has SPREAD to the scope's threshold. All three inputs already exist on the deed record.
howTitlesAreEarned.multiplicity: ⚠️ A PERSON MAY HOLD SEVERAL AT DIFFERENT SCOPES, and they may disagree. Being 'the Mercy of Thornwake' locally and 'the Grave-Caller' at domain scope is not a contradiction — it is the same person read by two audiences, and it is the best thing this system can produce.
howTitlesAreEarned.display: the title a person is introduced by is the one with the WIDEST scope KNOWN HERE — so a world title always lands, a domain title lands only among that tradition, and a local title only at home.

titles.name: The Grave-Caller
titles.note: ⚠️ THE TAIL, EARNED. Erik's own correction made this reachable: the Palelands' other half, and now a player can be it.

titles.name: The Easer
titles.note: The mode, not the tail. Both are Ashwarden titles and the tradition holds both without embarrassment.

titles.name: The Silencer
titles.note: They find the note of a heart and hold it until it stops.

titles.name: Of the Maw
titles.note: Not a name anyone gives themselves. It is what the traders call the ones who stopped trading.

titles.name: The Stripper
titles.note: Earned by unmaskings that cost the unmasked — the tail of truth-telling.

titles.name: The Quieter
titles.note: The calmest violence in the world, and the Stillhold do not disown them.

titles.name: The Reacher
titles.note: ⚠️ THREE RETRIEVALS IS A WORLD TITLE. Bringing someone back is rare enough that three makes you the person they send for.

titles.name: The Sealer
titles.note: ⚠️ ONE DEED. Sealing a retrievable person is the deed that travels furthest — and per Erik's ruling that player deeds travel, this is the one people repeat accurately.

titles.name: Kingmaker
titles.note: ⚠️ EARNED BY MAKING SOMEONE ELSE A LEGEND — the player's side of promotion-on-deeds. Two is enough because it is nearly impossible to do by accident.

titles.name: The Unbeaten
titles.note: The only title with a NEGATIVE condition — it is lost the first time you lose.

titles.name: Who Turned the ___
titles.note: ⚠️ NAMED FOR THE ARC — 'Who Turned the Bleed'. One is enough; a stage moving is a world event.

titles.name: The Kept Word
titles.note: Held mostly by people who are not otherwise remarkable, which is the point.

titles.name: Warden of the ___ Road
titles.note: Named for the road. A guard title, and it is regional because roads are.

titles.name: The One Who Is Owed
titles.note: Not admiration. People who are owed are known, and it is not always warm.

titles.name: A Hearth-Name
titles.note: ⚠️ THE MOST COMMON TITLE IN THE WORLD: ten good deeds in ONE place. Almost every long-played character earns one, and it is worth nothing anywhere else. That is not a weakness — it is what a home is.

titles.name: The Unwelcome
titles.note: The inverse, and it should exist. A place can decide about you.
titles.lostBy: leaving for a long enough time

designNotes: ⚠️ NO TITLE IS AWARDED FOR VIRTUE, per DIRECTIVE_SNG-280. Every one is earned by a COUNTED, TAGGED, SPREAD deed pattern. The Grave-Caller and the Easer sit at the same scope with the same thresholds; the Sealer is a world title and so is the Reacher. The world names what it notices, and it notices magnitude, not merit.

SCOPE IS REACH, NOT RANK. A hearth-name is not a lesser title than a world title — it is a title one place means. And a domain title is the strangest and best: known to your craft in reaches you have never visited, unknown to the farmers next door.
TITLES CAN CONTRADICT EACH OTHER AND SHOULD. 'The Mercy of Thornwake' locally and 'the Grave-Caller' at domain scope is one person read by two audiences.

THE TAILS ARE NOW PLAYER-REACHABLE. The modes-and-tails lore pass named what each tradition looks like at its far end; these titles are how a PLAYER arrives there — not by declaring it, but by being called it after the sixth time.
forCCode: deed tags: the `earnedBy.tags` above need emitting at the relevant moments (a retrieval succeeding, a sealing, a stage moved, a guard intercepting). Most are already recorded events looking for a tag.
scope resolution reads `deed.spread.length` and the regions those communities sit in — both already exist.

⚠️ DISPLAY RULE: introduce a person by the widest-scope title KNOWN IN THE CURRENT COMMUNITY. A world title always lands; a domain title lands only among that tradition; a hearth-name lands only at home. That single rule is what makes scope feel real rather than decorative.
AND SAY WHAT EARNED IT, per Erik's standing requirement: 'they have started calling you the Reacher on this side of the water.'
